Positioning

Self-care is already social. Very few rooms are built to hold it, and fewer still are licensed to treat you in one.

The problem

Wellness on the Westside is fragmented.

A patient optimizing their health today visits a medspa for injectables, a recovery studio for cold plunge, a longevity clinic for labs, and a concierge doctor for hormones. Four intakes, four records, four bills. Not one of them is somewhere you would choose to spend a Saturday morning.

4+

Separate providers a patient coordinates for care that belongs in one building.

24 of 30

Services on the L&K menu that require a physician, nurse practitioner or nurse. A recovery studio without a physician can offer 6.

10,488

US medical spas as of 2023, up from 8,899 the year before. The category is commoditizing on treatment alone.

The insight

Others proved the format.

Only a licensed facility can deliver it.

SWTHZ

Where a non-medical operator stops. No physician on site means no PRP, no IV therapy, no neuromodulators, no filler, no laser. Not features they skipped: the other side of a licensing threshold.

Soho House

Where the ladder was proven. Soho Friends is a published annual tier buying discounts and event invitations but no club access. What they lack is medicine.

The difference

L&K is not a practice built around a doctor. It is the facility a doctor needs.

The rooms, the diagnostics, the infusion suite, the staff and the accreditation, already standing. Physicians practice here, and investors own the building they practice in.

How the ladder fills

The open clinic is the top of the funnel.

Because anyone can book a procedure without joining, every non-member treatment is a paid introduction. The conversion path runs in one direction and each step is cheap to take.

Step one

Walks in

Books a procedure or buys a day pass. Pays list price. Owes nothing further.

Step two

Becomes a Friend

$300 a year pays for itself on roughly two procedures. Low friction, high volume, and it captures the database.

Step three

Becomes a Resident

Wants the circuit and the room, not just the treatment. This is where recurring revenue begins.

Step four

Becomes Longevity

Physician-delivered programming. Hard capped. The highest retention and the highest lifetime value in the building.

Equipment strategy

Purchased where payback justifies it. Wet areas drive cost: plunges, saunas and steam carry a materially higher per-SF buildout than a dry medspa, which is why the lean case trims the contrast suite before it trims treatment rooms.

Capacity

Enough capacity for what is sold.

Built bottom-up from station hours, not assumed. The circuit bottleneck is the cold plunge, not the sauna; the clinical bottleneck is treatment rooms.

73%

Recovery circuit utilization

2,345 modeled visits against 3,192 practical capacity, leaving 847 visits of headroom.

83%

Treatment room utilization

419 procedures against 507 practical capacity, leaving 88 slots of headroom.

76%

Red light utilization

650 sessions against 851 on 2 beds.

Practical capacity applies a utilization ceiling to theoretical station hours, because demand concentrates at peak times and nothing runs flat out. Headroom is the growth the facility can absorb without further capital.

Aligned Downside Protection.

The stake is priced against delivery. If the business underperforms, the investor owns more of it.

  • Investors start at 30%, priced against base-case stabilized operating income of $2.70M a year.
  • If trailing twelve-month operating income at stabilization lands below $2,200,000, ownership steps up on a straight line toward a hard cap of 40%, reached at the low case of $1,244,500.
  • At or above base case the investor stays at 30% and the founder keeps the upside. The ratchet only moves one way.
ScenarioOperating income /yrInvestor ownershipInvestor cash /yrFounder retained /yr
Low case$1,244,50040%$497,800$746,700
Base case$2,697,61130%$809,283$1,888,328
Upside case$4,150,72230%$1,245,217$2,905,505

In valuation terms the ratchet is exactly a halving of the pre-money, $11,083,333 to $7,125,000. It cushions the downside without making the investor whole: at the low case 40% of $1.24M is $497,800, still below the $809,283 that 30% of base case pays. Indicative terms, subject to definitive documents.

Investing Beyond Location One.

Playa Vista is the first building, and the terms treat it that way.

  • Location 1 is the proof of concept. It has to open, fill and stabilize before anything else is contemplated, and every figure in this brief describes that one building.
  • Round 1 investors receive pro-rata rights, not obligations, to invest in future locations at the same or improved terms, in proportion to their original stake. A 30% holder can maintain 30% of the platform without being required to.
  • Future locations target comparable high-income coastal and Westside markets, and only once Location 1 reaches stabilization.
  • The 25% expansion reserve on the capital page is what funds that optionality out of operating cash rather than out of a second raise. An investor who would rather take the cash can read the full-distribution column instead; the two are shown side by side because this is the actual trade.

No location beyond Playa Vista exists today. Pro-rata rights are a mechanism, not a pipeline, and are indicative terms subject to definitive documents.

How Investors Realize Value.

Three paths, in the order they are most likely to matter.

Buyback

The company holds a right, not an obligation, to repurchase investor equity in a defined window in years 3 to 5, priced off a formula tied to trailing twelve-month operating income at a multiple agreed in the definitive documents.

Right of first refusal

If a third-party offer for the business is received, existing investors get the first right to match it before any outside sale proceeds.

Strategic sale

The primary long-term path. Multi-location platforms trade at materially higher multiples than single-location assets, so the value of building a second and third location is realised at exit rather than only in operating cash.

Published EBITDA multiples
  • Single location, owner is primary provider3.5x to 5.0x
  • Single location, strong operator with SOPs5.0x to 6.5x
  • Multi-location, two or more with management6.0x to 7.5x
  • Multi-location, provider bench and recurring revenue7.0x to 9.0x
  • Membership revenue premium+0.5x to 1.0x

L&K runs 41.9% of revenue from memberships and access, above the 30% to 40% band that source names as a premium driver.

Multiples: Breakwater M&A, 20 February 2026. https://www.breakwaterma.com/blog/medical-spa-valuation-multiples-2026 · Industry M&A comparables, not company projections. The entry price on this round is 5.87x base-case operating income, inside the single-location band above and below every multi-location band.

What we are flagging before you ask.

  • Year 1 operating income is negative. Six of those months are construction and the rest are the opening ramp. There is no debt service to carry through it, and the $1,105,800 working capital reserve inside use of funds is sized against a modeled cash trough of $42,467 at month 9.
  • The reserve is deliberately larger than the trough it covers, 26.0 times over. With no lender there is no mandated reserve and no covenant to cure, so the cushion is a choice: it funds a materially slower ramp than the one modeled without a second raise. It is idle cash and we are naming it rather than leaving it to be found.
  • The ratchet cushions the downside without making the investor whole. At the low case 40% of $1.24M pays $497,800, which is still less than the $809,283 that 30% of base case pays. Every ownership percentage, valuation and buyback term in this brief is indicative and subject to definitive documents.
  • The multi-location expansion and platform exit thesis represent optionality this structure creates, not a guaranteed roadmap. No location beyond Playa Vista currently exists, and all forward-looking multiples are sourced from industry M&A comparables, not company-specific projections.
  • Volume is flexed to 72% of base in the low case and the business still produces $1.24M of annual operating income, with fixed overhead held constant. That is the conservative treatment: in a genuine downside you would cut staff before you cut the lease.
  • All forward-looking figures are projections on the stated assumptions and are not guarantees. Market and demographic figures carry their sources; anything unsourced was cut rather than estimated.

Healthcare administration and development

Co-founder

Roles included overseeing operations, finance, and practice management and development, as well as administration for a team of board-certified surgeons across orthopedics, spine, pain management, plastic surgery, and general surgery. Risks

What could go wrong, and what we did about it.

RiskMitigation
Membership fills slower than modeled.The clinic is open to non-members from day one, so revenue does not depend on the club filling. The low case flexes volume to 72% of base and still produces positive operating income.
Members redeem more than their fees cover.Credit banks are sized against measured redemption and the model asserts the ratio stays below 100%. The three-month minimum with 30-day change notice makes repricing operationally possible.
A key clinical seat turns over during the ramp.The asset is the facility, not any one clinician. The club layer, recovery floor and infusion suite run on materially less scarce staffing than the injectable and prescribing lines, so a temporary gap narrows the offering without closing the building. A licensed, equipped facility can credential a replacement. Clinical compensation carries retention terms through the ramp.
The ramp runs slower than modeled and the cash runs out.This is the risk that replaces financing risk when there is no lender. There is no payment to miss and no covenant to breach, so the only hard constraint is cash. The reserve is sized against the modeled trough, the low case still produces positive operating income at stabilization, and founding presales land during construction rather than after opening.
A national brand opens nearby.The defensible asset is the licensed facility, not the sauna. Adding injectables, infusions and physician oversight is not a product decision for a recovery studio: it means becoming a licensed medical facility, with the staffing, supervision, malpractice and accreditation that implies.
Wet-area construction overruns.The highest-variance line in the buildout. The lean case exists precisely as the fallback scope, and the reserve is sized against the modeled cash trough rather than to a round number.
